question: The reduction of 15% in the price of salt enables a person to buy 2 kg more for ₹272. The reduced price of salt per kg (in ₹) is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The reduction of price = 15%

A person can buy 2 kg more salt for ₹272.

The reduced price = (Price/Quantity) × (Reduction/100)

= (272/2) × (15/100) = 20.40

∴ The reduced price of salt per kg (in ₹) is ₹ 20.40

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The reduction of price = 15%

A person can buy 2 kg more salt for ₹272.

**Calculation:**

Let, the original price of the salt = ₹ x/kg

The person can buy = 272/x kg

The price of salt after reduced = x × (85/100) = 17x/20

So, (272)/(17x/20)-(272)/(x)=2

⇒ ((272×20)-(272×17))/(17x)=2

⇒ 272 (20 - 17) = 34x

⇒ 272 × 3 = 34x

⇒ x = (272 × 3)/34 = 24

The original price of the salt = 24/kg

The reduced price = (85/100) × 24 = ₹ 20.40 per kg

**∴ The reduced price of salt per kg (in ₹) is ₹ 20.40**
